newsitem.title: USA: U.S. industrial output rises despite loss of jobs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. industrial output rises despite loss of jobs.

text.p: September's decline in manufacturing jobs held industrial production to marginal gains in the month but the manufacturing outook was sanguine, economists said.

"We know from the employment data that the manufacturing sector of the economy slowed significantly in the month of September," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. "But if anything (the report) suggests production was in line with expectations or maybe a touch stronger."

The Federal Reserve said industrial production rose 0.2 percent in September, while capacity utilization moderated to 83.3 from a revised 83.4 in August. Excluding motor vehicles and parts, industrial production rose 0.4 percent.
The average forecast in a Reuters survey said production would rise by 0.1 percent and that capacity use would decline to 83.3 from previously reported 83.5.

While the data was up, Jobnson said there was little indication that production will overheat. The numbers are simply "as flat as they can get," he said, conceding the drop in auto production may have been strike or weather related.
Marilyn Schaja, money market economist at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette Securities Corp, also said the slightly stronger production reading was innocuous and the markets would embrace the data.
"There were no real surprises in the report at all," Schaja said, adding that it continues to be good news in that it does not suggest significant capacity constraints.

Regarding the bigger picture, Christopher Rupkey, financial economist at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, said growth is positive but it pales next to the brisk pace seen earlier this year. First half production growth averaged 4.5 percent, he noted.
"(Production) is probably going to be much weaker in the fourth quarter and it's doing exactly what the Fed wants," Rupkey said. "They may stay on the sidelines."
